title: APPLIED — Plaintiff applied through Indeed for the Night Auditor / Guest Service Agent position at Delta Hotels by Marriott Santa Clara–Silicon Valley.
INTERVIEW — In-person interview at the Hotel conducted by John Barros.

OFFER AND SCREENING PACKET — Denet Venegas emailed the written offer ($24/hr Night Audit; $23/hr GSA) and the Universal Background Screening packet on the 'Delta Santa Clara' trade name. The authorization recites separate DISCLOSURE documents; none was provided. Plaintiff returned the signed offer and authorization the same day.

MARRIOTT CREDENTIALS — Marriott Systems Support emailed Venegas and Plaintiff that his Marriott Enterprise ID was created (request CSEID4637520); the email states it contains information from Marriott International, Inc.
MARRIOTT ASSOCIATE RATE — Marriott verified Plaintiff for Explore by Marriott Bonvoy (Explore Associate rate).

HOWELL REMARK — During Night Audit training, Howell remarked 'He released you didn't he?' referring to released sex offenders. The Nov. 1–7 roster cutting Plaintiff's overnights from 4 to 3 was already posted when Plaintiff arrived for the shift.
FIRST CUT DOCUMENTED — Plaintiff photographed the posted Nov. 1–7 roster (3 overnights).
PROGRESS REPORT — Plaintiff texted Barros that he could perform about 70% of Night Audit tasks without help. The roster was not changed.
CALL-OUT — Plaintiff called Howell (no answer; Howell was off) and texted him that he could not attend that night's training.
BARROS 'HEARD' — Barros texted Plaintiff about his attendance, saying he had 'heard' about it.
SECOND CUT — Barros sent the next roster reducing Plaintiff to 2 overnights; Nov. 5–6 and Nov. 12–14 front-desk shifts went to Thao Truong and Bretado.
HOWELL ADMISSION — Howell told Plaintiff: 'Well, it's because you've been calling out of your shifts. That's why John has been scheduling you less and less.'

WRITTEN WARNING — Barros issued a written warning (lowest level) reciting only Plaintiff's 11:01, 11:05, and 11:21 texts to Howell; both signed and Barros kept the copies. Asked whether the cuts from 4 to 3 to 2 were by design, Barros said: 'It is by design. It is by design. It is by design.'
PARTIAL RESTORATION — Barros sent an updated roster with 3 overnights (Nov. 17–19), during 100% occupancy Nov. 16–18.

COMPLAINT v22 DRAFTED — Federal complaint (N.D. Cal., San Jose) with Marriott International, Inc. as lead caption defendant; § 290.46(j) cat's paw, FCRA § 1681b(b)(2)(A), and ICRAA § 1786.16 counts; Nov. 17 Westlaw verification findings applied. Unfiled.
